records.name: Broken Inheritance
records.definition: A subclass that violates its base type's contract, for example by an override that changes the expected inputs or outputs, so substituting it breaks callers that rely on the base behavior.

records.name: Fat Interface

distinctFrom.reason: A fat interface bundles unrelated operations for its clients, while a repository dump is a repository grown into a second service layer.

records.definition: An interface bundling many unrelated operations, forcing clients to depend on methods they never call.

records.name: Switch-Based Extension
records.definition: Extending behavior by editing a growing switch or conditional on a type instead of adding a new polymorphic type.

records.name: Type Switching
records.definition: Branching on an object's concrete type instead of dispatching through a shared polymorphic interface or a visitor's double dispatch.

records.name: Consumer-Specific Contracts
records.definition: The ability to give each client an interface exposing only the operations it uses.

records.name: Feature Extension without Modification
records.definition: The ability to add new behavior by writing new code rather than editing existing, tested code.

records.name: Contract Preservation

distinctFrom.reason: Contract preservation binds a subtype to all of its base type's guarantees, while an invariant is one guarantee that holds in every state.
Contract preservation binds a subtype to every guarantee, while a postcondition is the one an operation gives on return.
Contract preservation binds a subtype to every guarantee, while a precondition is what an operation needs before it runs.

records.definition: The requirement that a subtype honor every behavioral guarantee of the type it replaces.

records.name: Role-Specific Interfaces
records.definition: The requirement that interfaces be defined per client role rather than as one general-purpose surface.

records.name: Interface Proliferation
records.definition: The degree to which splitting interfaces finely multiplies the number of small interfaces to manage.

records.name: Narrow Specialized Behavior
records.definition: The degree to which honoring a base type's contract constrains a subtype from specializing its own behavior.

records.name: Extract Interface
records.definition: A technique for declaring the operations clients use as an interface, so the clients depend on it instead of on the class.

records.name: Extract Role Interface
records.definition: A technique for splitting the operations one client role uses into an interface of their own.

records.name: Split Interface
records.definition: A technique for dividing a broad interface into smaller ones, each holding operations that change together.

records.name: Replace Inheritance with Delegation
records.definition: A technique for replacing a subclass with a class that holds the former base as a field and forwards to it.

records.name: Split Hierarchy
records.definition: A technique for dividing a class hierarchy whose subtypes do not honor one contract into hierarchies that each do.

records.name: Invert Dependency
records.definition: A technique for making a high-level module own an abstraction that a low-level module implements.
